model_metrics.best_model: Blend: 0.5 * GBM-log(+transfer) + 0.5 * persistence (50/50 weight fixed in advance, not tuned on test)

caveats: Mean-3yr is unusually weak in 2025 because 2023 was a record outbreak (321,593 cases) that inflates the 3-year mean; the baseline over-predicts the 2025 annual total by +57.5%. Beating it in 2025 is easier than in a normal year. The model's absolute error (MAE ~8.6 cases/district-week, annual error +0.2%) is the stronger evidence.

Persistence (last week = this week) is a strong 1-week-ahead naive forecast (MAE 9.42) and slightly beats the GBM alone (9.55). The blend beats both (8.61). The GBM's edge over persistence is at turning points (top-10% change weeks: GBM 50.4 vs persistence 57.2) and in MAPE (66% vs 78%).
Transfer-learning (stage-1) features added almost nothing to the GBM (9.55 vs 9.59 MAE) but clearly helped the LSTM (11.31 vs 11.84 MAE; annual +1.3% vs -8.6%).
1-week-ahead forecasts only, using observed history. Multi-week-ahead skill was not tested.
MAPE is high (~66%) because many district-weeks have tiny counts, where small absolute errors are large in percentage terms.

The dghs_division_daily.csv file could not be used as a weekly pretraining series (75% of new_admissions NaN; only 139 complete weeks, all in 2026). Division-weekly data was built by aggregating the observed district-weekly file, so the stage-1 division model is a hierarchical / stacking component, not independent pretraining data.
Four year-boundary weeks in the Figshare file are all-zero artefacts (2019-08-26, 2022-12-26, 2024-12-30, 2025-12-29) and were masked as missing, never trained on or evaluated.
No estimated district cases (master file) were used as targets anywhere. All targets are observed Figshare district-week cases.
